hints.title: Table Row Combination
hints.text: When two tables share identical columns, they can be joined vertically into a unified table. Which top-level function combines sequence collections along a designated axis?

hints.title: Axis Orientation for Stacking
hints.text: The pd.concat function accepts a list of DataFrames and an axis parameter where axis=0 performs vertical row stacking.

hints.title: Concatenation Call Formulation
hints.text: Return pd.concat([df1, df2], axis=0) to combine the records of both tables into a continuous vertical dataset.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Linear block concatenation copying memory buffers into the combined structure.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Appending row by row or using deprecated append in loops produces quadratic copying overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Allocating the concatenated DataFrame requires memory proportional to combined input size.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct usage of pd.concat with explicit axis=0 handling index preservation.
